authoredPrompt: This figure shows one undirected weighted graph in which a spanning tree has been picked out by shading. Nine circular vertices carry italic letters: b, c, and d sit across the top, e at the right, f at the lower right, g along the bottom, h at the lower left, a at the left, and i in the middle. Fourteen straight edges join them, each annotated with an integer weight: a-b is 4, b-c is 8, c-d is 7, d-e is 9, a-h is 8, b-h is 11, h-i is 7, h-g is 1, g-i is 6, i-c is 2, c-f is 4, g-f is 2, d-f is 14, and e-f is 10. Eight of those edges, namely a-b, b-c, c-d, d-e, c-i, c-f, h-g, and g-f, are drawn with a broad gray band running behind the line, while the other six remain thin black strokes. The shading is what the reader compares against: it marks an acyclic subset that still reaches every vertex, so the weights along it can be summed and weighed against the heavier unshaded edges it leaves out. The drawing supplies a concrete instance of the wiring problem, in which pins are vertices, possible interconnections are edges, and an edge weight is the amount of wire needed to make that connection.
authoredInteractions:
- Click for selecting any edge: the chosen edge highlights with its weight and whether it is in the shaded tree, making clear how individual edge choices affect cycles, connectivity, and total cost.
- Toggle between the shown spanning tree and the alternate tree that swaps b-c for a-h: the gray band moves while the total remains 37, making clear why a minimum spanning tree need not be unique.
- Button for stepping through the shaded-tree edges: each press adds one edge, updates the running weight, and marks reached vertices, making clear how an acyclic set can still span all vertices.
authoredContext: We can model this wiring problem with a connected, undirected graph G D .V; E/, where V is the set of pins, E is the set of possible interconnections between pairs of pins, and for each edge .u; _x0017_/ 2 E, we have a weight w.u; _x0017_/ specifying the cost (amount of wire needed) to connect u and _x0017_. We then wish to find an acyclic subset T _x0012_ E that connects all of the vertices and whose total weight w.T / D X .u;_x0017_/2T w.u; _x0017_/ is minimized. Since T is acyclic and connects all of the vertices, it must form a tree, which we call a spanning tree since it “spans” the graph G. We call the problem of determining the tree T the minimum-spanning-tree problem. 1 Figure 23.1 shows an example of a connected graph and a minimum spanning tree.

discrepancies: Default render shows a gray highlight band on EVERY edge; the source shades only the 8 minimum-spanning-tree edges. refreshBands() is defined but never called at startup, and every band is created with opacity 0.85, so the defining 'which edges are in the tree' distinction is absent until the user interacts.

The step walk's treeOrder contains 'i,c' and 'c,i', which both resolve (after sorting) to the same i-c edge, and omits b-c entirely: the walk adds only 7 unique tree edges, double-counts i-c, ends at a running weight of 31 (not 37), yet the final narration claims 'an acyclic set of 8 edges spans the graph'.
Hardcoded treeOrder is keyed to the default tree, so stepping after toggling the 'Alternate tree' checkbox walks edges (a-b) that may no longer be in the displayed tree.
evaluation.notes: Vertex positions, edge topology, and all labels match the source exactly, but a missing refreshBands() call at init shades every edge (erasing the MST highlight, the figure's entire point) and the edge-walk double-counts i-c while omitting b-c, producing a wrong 31 total under a narration that claims a correct 8-edge spanning tree.
action_items: Call refreshBands() once at startup (before __markRendered()) so only tree edges are shaded in the default view.

Fix treeOrder: replace the duplicate 'c,i' entry with 'b,c' so the walk adds each of the 8 tree edges exactly once and the running total reaches 37; make the final narration consistent with the actual unique-edge count.
Disable or remap the 'Add next tree edge' walk when the Alternate tree checkbox is active, since the hardcoded order no longer matches the displayed tree.
